subject: Pilot ingest gap analysis & RPS contour — POC plan and owners
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rivera <elena@novalytics.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos@novalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Pilot ingest gap analysis & RPS contour — POC plan and owners

Hi Elena / Carlos —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the concrete requests we discussed to get the pilot scoped and scheduled. I captured what I have below; please correct anything I misunderstood.

Call highlights (brief):
- Primary use case: conversational support + long-context summarization for customer tickets.
- Traffic pattern: small steady baseline with periodic high bursts around peak support windows.
- Key constraints: PII redaction requirement, data retention 30 days, and internal audit logging.

What we need to move to a scoped POC:
1) Traffic snapshot (CSV) with RPS/time-series, example tokens-per-request, and sample concurrency during peak 15-min windows. Attached is a simple ingest_template.csv you can fill.
2) Confirm success criteria: latency (p95) target, acceptable error/quality delta vs current baseline, and cost guardrail.
3) Owners and timeline: propose Redwood owner (Aditya) for infra and Marissa for telemetry; Novalytics owner for data prep and test harness.

Initial assumptions we made on the call — please confirm or correct:
- Average token length per request: ~180 tokens (text only).
- Typical sustained RPS baseline: 4–6 RPS.
- Peak bursts: up to ~120 RPS for 1–3 minute windows during morning and end-of-day flushes.
- Concurrent sessions: ~25–40.

Proposed next steps (mutual action items):
- Novalytics: share anonymized traffic snapshot (see ingest_template.csv) by end of day Wednesday (18 Nov).
- Redwood: produce an initial POC config and cost estimate within 48 hours of receiving snapshot.
- Both: align on success criteria doc and sign-off on POC start date.

Attachments: ingest_template.csv (CSV template)

Thanks — I can host a short sync if you want to walk through the CSV after you export it.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com

----

From: Elena Rivera <elena@novalytics.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos@novalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot ingest gap analysis & RPS contour — POC plan and owners

Hey Nikhil —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items and attaching a short traffic snapshot (anonymized) from last month: novalytics_traffic_snapshot.csv. Key notes from our side:
- Average RPS: 3–5 (comfortable baseline).
- Peak bursts: we see spikes to ~110–130 RPS but typically for 60–180 seconds. The largest burst last month hit ~210 RPS for ~45s during a campaign.
- Token lengths: median ~150, mean ~210, 90th percentile ~920 tokens (we have some very long threads in the CRM).
- Concurrency: 20–35 active sessions during peak.

Questions from our engineering lead:
1) Can Redwood provide recommendations for a quantization/config profile given the 900+ token tail?
2) What observability hooks do you need to validate prefix/KV cache effectiveness for our workload?

We'll aim to get the CSV cleaned and uploaded by end of day Wednesday as requested. If you prefer, I can drop the export into the Drive link you shared.

Attachment: novalytics_traffic_snapshot.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Regards,
Elena Rivera
Head of Product Engineering — Novalytics
elena@novalytics.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rivera <elena@novalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Pilot ingest gap analysis & RPS contour — POC plan and owners

Elena —

Appreciate the snapshot and context. Below is a compact POC evaluation plan based on the data you shared and our internal assumptions. If that looks good, we'll lock dates.

Redwood proposed POC evaluation plan (2-week pilot):
- Prep (3 business days): ingest sample, configure model variant and quantization recommendation, connect telemetry. Owner: Novalytics (data export) + Aditya (infra).
- Baseline run (3 days): run with conservative batch sizes and no KV caching to measure raw latency/cost. Success metric: p95 latency < 350ms on baseline smaller requests; track cost per 1k tokens.
- Optimized run (7 days): enable prefix/KV caching, dynamic batching tuned to your RPS shape, and recommended quantization. Success metric: overall P95 < 300ms for baseline requests, tail (90th) kept under 1s for long-context cases; cache hit rate > 40%.
- Quality gating: run 100 synthetic prompts (edge cases you supply) each week; quality delta must be within agreed threshold (we'll propose a 3% top-level regression cap).
- Final readout (1 day): summarize latency, cost delta, cache effectiveness, and recommended production configuration.

POC timeline (proposed):
- Nov 18: Novalytics uploads full snapshot and sample prompts.
- Nov 19–21: Redwood config + dry run.
- Nov 22–Dec 5: Pilot window (data collection).
- Dec 6: Readout and next-steps decision.

Action items (owners):
- Novalytics: upload final anonymized CSV + 100 sample prompts (Elena).
- Redwood infra: initial config and cost estimate (Aditya).
- Redwood telemetry: integrate trace and token-level metrics (Marissa).
- Redwood AE: coordinate weekly check-ins and final readout (Nikhil).

Technical notes / recommendations:
- For the 900-token tail, recommend a 16-bit quantization profile and explicit KV-cache for repeated context. We'll provide a recommended kernel/quant profile post-snapshot.
- Batching window: dynamic, with a 20–50ms max wait depending on live RPS — this should reduce per-token CPU while preserving p95 targets.

Attachment: redwood_poc_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

If this plan looks good, I'll share a calendar invite for the kickoff on Nov 22 and open a shared Drive folder for artifacts.

Thanks —
Nikhil
